note: Condition Field defines a field type 'condition_field' (default widget condition_field_default, formatter condition_field_string) that stores core Condition plugin configurations as a serialized 'conditions' blob. Which condition plugins are offered per field is the field setting enabled_plugins (schema field.field_settings.condition_field). The module does not evaluate conditions; ConditionAccessResolver::checkAccess($conditions,'and'|'or') is the helper. No configure route, permissions, or Drush. Medium reads back the enabled_plugins of a known field; hard adds a condition_field to Article with request_path + user_role enabled, verified against the live field config. Fixture fields are namespaced field_cf_*.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal condition_field module provide, and what is the machine name of its field type? Does it evaluate the conditions itself?
evals.expected_output: It provides a field type with machine name condition_field that stores core Condition plugin configurations on an entity (default widget condition_field_default, formatter condition_field_string). It does NOT evaluate them itself — you read the field and resolve the conditions in your own code.

evals.prompt: When adding a condition_field field to a content type, how do I control which condition plugins editors can configure on it, and what is that field setting called?
evals.expected_output: The field settings form has 'Enabled plugins' checkboxes; the setting is enabled_plugins (schema field.field_settings.condition_field), a map of condition-plugin id => enabled. Some plugins are always skipped (SKIP_CONDITION_IDS: node_type, current_theme, webform, entity_bundle:webform_submission, and language on monolingual sites).

evals.prompt: I have data stored in a condition_field field. How do I actually evaluate those stored conditions in code (e.g. to hide an entity), using the helper the module ships?
evals.expected_output: Read $entity->get('field')->getValue()[0]['conditions'], instantiate each via plugin.manager.condition ($manager->createInstance($id, $values)), then call ConditionAccessResolver::checkAccess($conditions, 'and'|'or') (returns bool). Do it in e.g. hook_entity_view to blank out $build when it returns FALSE.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has a condition_field field. Inspect the live field configuration and give the field's machine name and which condition plugins are enabled on it (enabled_plugins).
evals.expected_output: The field is field_cf_known (type condition_field on node.article); its enabled_plugins setting enables request_path and user_role (drush cget field.field.node.article.field_cf_known settings.enabled_plugins).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, add a Condition Field (condition_field) named field_cf_task to the Article content type, with the Request Path (request_path) and Role (user_role) condition plugins enabled on it. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A field storage (node, field_cf_task, type condition_field) and a field config on node.article exist, with settings.enabled_plugins enabling request_path and user_role (FieldStorageConfig + FieldConfig create, or Field UI).
